title: Integration and comparison of a positive ray of torus weights
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $\mathbf G_a$ and $\mathbf G_m$ for the group schemes of [def-sc-gm-ga]. The Lie algebra of a group is its tangent space at the identity. A smooth affine group is unipotent if every geometric point is a unipotent matrix in a faithful finite-dimensional linear representation. Let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type. Let $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ be a split torus acting on $H$ by group-scheme automorphisms. Put $X^*(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,\mathbf G_m)$, written additively, and let $\mathfrak h_\chi$ denote the $\chi$-weight subspace for the differentiated $S$-action on $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$; thus the weight is a character, not its differential. For a nonzero character $\eta$, put $R_\eta=\{\chi\in X^*(S):m\chi=n\eta\text{ for some integers }m,n>0\}$ and $V_\eta=\bigoplus_{\chi\in R_\eta}\mathfrak h_\chi$. There is a smooth connected unipotent closed subgroup $U_\eta\subseteq H$, stable under $S$, with $\operatorname{Lie}(U_\eta)=V_\eta$. For every smooth connected $S$-stable closed subgroup $K\subseteq H$ one has
$$V_\eta\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(K)\ \Longrightarrow\ U_\eta\subseteq K,\qquad \operatorname{Lie}(K)\subseteq V_\eta\ \Longrightarrow\ K\subseteq U_\eta.$$
In particular $U_\eta$ is the unique such smooth connected $S$-stable closed subgroup with tangent space $V_\eta$.

source.place: Proposition 16.64 and the immediately following uniqueness sentence, printed pp.348--349; unipotence follows from Proposition 16.62, printed pp.346--347, since this positive-ray tangent space has no zero weight. The action may be external, as throughout Section 16i.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] to identify $S=D_F(X)$ with $X=X^*(S)\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] over $\mathbf Z$ to $N=\mathbf Z\eta\subseteq O=X$. Since $\eta\ne0$, the map $\mathbf Z\to N$, $a\mapsto a\eta$, is an isomorphism, so the basis of $N$ has one element, necessarily $\eta$ or $-\eta$. Changing the sign of the corresponding ambient basis vector gives a basis $(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r)$ of $X$ with $\eta=d\epsilon_1$, $d>0$. Antiduality gives coordinates $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ with $\epsilon_i(t)=t_i$. Put $T=\{t_1=1\}\simeq\mathbf G_m^{r-1}$ and $\lambda(t)=(t,1,\ldots,1)$. A character $\chi=\sum_i b_i\epsilon_i$ is trivial on $T$ precisely when $b_i=0$ for $i>1$. In that case $\chi\lambda(t)=t^{b_1}$, and $\chi\in R_\eta$ precisely when $b_1>0$: the defining equation is $mb_1=nd$ with $m,n>0$.

source.place: p.348, character line and its subtorus; Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234. Smith normal form makes the primitive-coordinate choice explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] successively to the $r$ commuting coordinate copies of $\mathbf G_m$ in $S$. After decomposing under the first $j$ factors, every summand is preserved by the remaining factors: a commuting action carries a vector of prescribed first $j$ weights to a vector with those same weights. Decomposing each summand under factor $j+1$ therefore refines the direct sum. Starting with the whole space at $j=0$ proves the character decomposition for the differentiated action on $\mathfrak h$ and on any $S$-stable tangent subspace $\mathfrak k$. On the summand indexed by $(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$, the character is $\prod_i t_i^{b_i}$. Consequently $(\mathfrak h^T)_{\lambda,>0}=V_\eta$, and for an $S$-stable closed subgroup $K$ one has $(\mathfrak k^T)_{\lambda,>0}=\mathfrak k\cap V_\eta$. All weights are group characters; no differentiation of the integers $b_i$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, pp.234--235; p.348, formula (123).

proof.text: Form $G=H\rtimes S$, whose underlying scheme is $H\times_F S$ and whose product is $(h,s)(h\prime,s\prime)=(h(s\cdot h\prime),ss\prime)$. These regular maps and the inverse $(h,s)^{-1}=(s^{-1}\cdot h^{-1},s^{-1})$ satisfy the group laws by the action identities. The projection $H\times S\to H$ is smooth by [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection], and composing it with the smooth structure morphism of $H$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. For every field extension $L/F$, the coordinate ring of $S_L$ is $L[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, an integral domain; hence $S$ is geometrically connected. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components], $H\times S$ is connected because $H$ is connected. It is affine and of finite type from the displayed product coordinate algebra. The same construction and reasoning apply with any smooth connected $S$-stable closed subgroup $K$ in place of $H$.

source.place: Section 16i, external torus actions; the semidirect-product device also appears in the proof of Proposition 16.62, p.347. Product facts: Stacks Tag 0385 and smooth composition.

proof.text: Embed $T$ in $G$ by $t\mapsto(e,t)$ and apply [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected]. Its hypotheses hold by step 3; over algebraically closed $F$, connectedness is the geometric connectedness required there. Thus $C=C_G(T)$ is a smooth connected closed affine group. Direct calculation of commutation shows, on every test algebra and after every scalar extension, $$C(A)=\{(h,s):t\cdot h=h\text{ for all }t\in T(A\prime),\ A\prime/A\}\ .$$ There is no condition on $s$, since $S$ is commutative. A tangent vector at $(e,1)$ is a pair $(v,w)\in\mathfrak h\oplus\operatorname{Lie}(S)$. Applying this same equation over dual numbers gives $\operatorname{Lie}(C)=\mathfrak h^T\oplus\operatorname{Lie}(S)$. Conjugation by $(e,\lambda(t))$ acts by $\lambda(t)$ on the first summand and trivially on the second. Replacing $H$ by $K$ gives $C_K=C_{K\rtimes S}(T)$ with exactly the corresponding formulas, and its natural inclusion into $C$ is closed.

source.place: p.348, group fixed by the character-kernel torus and formula (123); Theorem 17.38, p.363, applied in the semidirect product; tangent invariants computed by the fixed-functor equation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] to $C$ and the cocharacter $t\mapsto(e,\lambda(t))$. Let $U$ be its contracting subgroup. It is smooth, connected, unipotent and closed in $C$. Its projection to $S$ is trivial: the projected orbit of $(h,s)$ is the constant $s$, while a contracting orbit has limit $(e,1)$. Thus $U$ is a closed subgroup of the kernel $H$ of $G\to S$. Steps 2 and 4 and the positive-weight tangent formula in the cited node give $\operatorname{Lie}(U)=V_\eta$. Conjugation by $(e,s)$ for $s\in S$ preserves $C$, commutes with $\lambda$, and preserves the identity limit; hence it preserves $U$ as a subgroup functor. Set $U_\eta=U$. Applying the same cited theorem in $C_K$ defines a smooth connected closed subgroup $U_K\subseteq K$, with $\operatorname{Lie}(U_K)=\mathfrak k\cap V_\eta$. Its inclusion into $U_\eta$ follows on all test algebras: an orbit extending in the closed subgroup $C_K$ also extends in $C$ with the same identity limit.

source.place: p.348, definition U_(alpha) and description (124); Theorem 13.33(a),(c),(e), pp.265--266. Unipotence is already included in the cited cocharacter node.

proof.text: Assume $V_\eta\subseteq\mathfrak k$. Then $\operatorname{Lie}(U_K)=\mathfrak k\cap V_\eta=V_\eta=\operatorname{Lie}(U_\eta)$. The inclusion $U_K\to U_\eta$ is $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant for $\lambda$, fixes the identity, and has isomorphic differential. Both schemes are smooth connected affine of finite type by step 5. Every source tangent weight is strictly positive by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-equivariant-inverse] to conclude that this inclusion is an isomorphism. Therefore $U_\eta=U_K\subseteq K$ as closed subgroup schemes.

source.place: Proposition 16.64(a), p.348; Corollary 13.42, p.270, replaces the same-dimension conclusion by a directly applicable equivariant inverse criterion.

proof.text: Assume instead $\mathfrak k\subseteq V_\eta$. Then $\operatorname{Lie}(U_K)=\mathfrak k$, so the closed inclusion $U_K\to K$ has isomorphic differential. It is equivariant for $\lambda$ and fixes the identity. The source and target are smooth connected affine of finite type, and the source tangent weights are all strictly positive. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-equivariant-inverse] again, now to $U_K\to K$, obtaining $K=U_K\subseteq U_\eta$. This proves the second comparison directly without asserting that the Lie algebra of a generated subgroup equals the Lie algebra generated by its inputs. If the common tangent space is zero, the same cited criterion explicitly allows the empty set of weights.

source.place: Proposition 16.64(b), p.348, with Corollary 13.42, p.270, in place of the abbreviated generated-subgroup argument.

proof.text: If a smooth connected $S$-stable closed subgroup $L\subseteq H$ has $\operatorname{Lie}(L)=V_\eta$, both proved implications apply to $L$ and give $U_\eta\subseteq L\subseteq U_\eta$. Thus $L=U_\eta$. This includes the case $V_\eta=0$; no nonzero tangent weight is assumed to occur.

source.place: p.349, uniqueness sentence immediately following Proposition 16.64.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 16.64, pp.348--349, using the explicit character-kernel/cocharacter construction. Both comparisons use Corollary 13.42, p.270; this supplies a scheme-theoretic argument for the abbreviated comparison proof.

Statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Checked against Milne iAG2017 pp.348-349 (16.64 with (123)-(125)) and 13.41/13.42 (pp.269-270). The route is Milne's: T_eta is the kernel torus of the character line and U is the contracting subgroup of its centralizer. Two legitimate changes: it uses the internal centralizer C_{H x| S}(T)=H^T x| S, and it applies Cor 13.42 twice in place of Milne's abbreviated dimension and generated-subgroup arguments. Step 1: Smith with N=Z eta in X gives eta=d eps_1 with d>0; I checked that R_eta is exactly b_1>0 with b_i=0 for i>1. Step 2: weight decomposition by group characters, valid in char p. Step 3: smoothness via the torus projection plus composition, connectedness via Stacks 0385. Step 4: conjugation (e,t)(h,s)(e,t)^-1=(t.h,s) gives C=H^T x| S and Lie C=h^T+Lie S; geometric connectedness holds because kbar=F. Step 5: the limit forces s=1, so U lies in H; Lie U=V_eta and Lie U_K=k cap V_eta; S-stable; U_K is in U_eta. Steps 6-7: the equivariant-inverse node (I checked it is true: graded Nakayama plus Krull intersection, connectedness needed) applied to U_K->U_eta and to U_K->K. Step 8 is elementary. New node lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases is an exact Mathlib leaf, Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le, PID.lean 492-497; not a duplicate (the DVR and full-rank Smith nodes are special cases). Edge cases checked: r=0, V_eta=0, G_a with weight p in char p, and negative multiples. Batch-5: torus-projection and smooth-composition are generic scheme facts; antiduality reaches trf only via exterior/dual base change of projective modules; the centralizer reaches trf only via a geometric-connectedness criterion. None is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so all are accepted. All three declared tool_uses accepted. No SGA. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_torus_positiveRay_subgroup (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (H S : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [IsAffine H.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom] [Smooth H.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace H.X.left] (r : ℕ) (hS : Nonempty (S ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) [ModObj S.X H.X] (hAut : ActsByGroupAutomorphisms S H) (eta : S ⟶ Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative F)) (heta : eta.hom.hom ≠ 1) : ∃ (U : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (i : U ⟶ H), IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ Smooth U.X.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace U.X.left ∧ SolvableGroupStructure.IsUnipotent U ∧ IsStable S H i ∧ (GrpObj.differential i.hom.hom).toLinearMap.range = positiveRaySpace S H eta ∧ (∀ (K : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (j : K ⟶ H), IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → Smooth K.X.hom → ConnectedSpace K.X.left → IsStable S H j → (positiveRaySpace S H eta ≤ (GrpObj.differential j.hom.hom).toLinearMap.range → ∃ f : U ⟶ K, f ≫ j = i) ∧ ((GrpObj.differential j.hom.hom).toLinearMap.range ≤ positiveRaySpace S H eta → ∃ f : K ⟶ U, f ≫ i = j)) ∧ (∀ (K : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (j : K ⟶ H), IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → Smooth K.X.hom → ConnectedSpace K.X.left → IsStable S H j → (GrpObj.differential j.hom.hom).toLinearMap.range = positiveRaySpace S H eta → ∃ e : K ≅ U, e.hom ≫ i = j)

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches Milne Prop 16.64 and its uniqueness sentence clause by clause. InPositiveRay is m chi = n eta with m,n>0; positiveRaySpace is the sup underlying the direct sum.
